title: Short Stuff: Birthday Paradox
summary: Short Stuff episode on the birthday problem (often called the birthday paradox). Josh opens with a personal story about sharing a birthday with his daughter-era anecdote and Chuck's birthday, then the hosts explain that the chance of a shared birthday grows exponentially with group size rather than linearly. They walk through the pairings math (23 people give 253 pairings, roughly a 50 percent chance of a match; 70 people give over 99 percent), cite a HowStuffWorks article by Laurie Dove and a mathematician named Frost, and close with a penny-doubling example showing exponential growth (about ten million dollars after thirty days, which they say is ten point seven million).
topics: Stuff You Should Know Short Stuff

segments.title: Opening banter and birthday anecdote
segments.summary: Josh introduces the topic and tells a story about learning that he and Chuck share a birthday, and his later effort to get Chuck listed on Famous Birthdays.

segments.title: Introducing the birthday problem
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the chance of two people in a room sharing a birthday is 1 in 364 for a pair, but the odds grow exponentially as more people are added, so the name is the birthday problem rather than a true paradox.

segments.title: Calculating the odds of shared birthdays
segments.summary: The hosts pose the question of how many random people are needed for a shared birthday, then explain counting pairings: 5 people give 10 pairings, 23 people give 253 pairings, and multiplying the non-matching probabilities gives about a 50.17 percent chance of a match with 23 people. They also note that 70 people give over 99 percent.

segments.title: Penny doubling example of exponential growth
segments.summary: Using a mathematician named Frost as a source, the hosts illustrate exponential growth with an offer of one penny on day one, two on day two, and so on for thirty days, which they say comes to about ten point seven million dollars.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the episode and sign off with the show credit.
